### lam/math/color.h

```cpp
#include <lam/math/color.h>
```

Source: [`src/math/include/lam/math/color.h`](../src/math/include/lam/math/color.h). Namespaces: `lam`.

8-bit RGBA colour.

#### struct `Color`

```cpp
struct Color {
    std::uint8_t r = 255, g = 255, b = 255, a = 255;
    // Color::hex(0xRRGGBBAA).
    static constexpr Color hex(std::uint32_t rrggbbaa);
    constexpr Color with_alpha(std::uint8_t alpha) const;
    constexpr bool operator==(const Color &) const = default;
};
```

```cpp
inline constexpr Color kWhite{255, 255, 255, 255};
inline constexpr Color kBlack{0, 0, 0, 255};
inline constexpr Color kTransparent{0, 0, 0, 0};
```

```cpp
Color lerp(Color a, Color b, float t);
```

Channel-wise lerp, t clamped to [0, 1], rounded to nearest.

```cpp
Color multiply(Color a, Color b);
```

Channel-wise product (a \* b / 255), rounded.

```cpp
Color scale_alpha(Color c, float factor);
```

Alpha times factor; factor clamped to [0, 1].

```cpp
float luma(Color c);
```

Perceived brightness 0..1 (Rec. 601 weights).

### lam/math/curve.h

```cpp
#include <lam/math/curve.h>
```

Source: [`src/math/include/lam/math/curve.h`](../src/math/include/lam/math/curve.h). Namespaces: `lam`.

Keyframed colour over a wrapping [0, 1) domain, e.g. time-of-day ambient light.

#### struct `ColorKey`

```cpp
struct ColorKey {
    float t = 0;
    Color color;
};
```

#### class `ColorCurve`

```cpp
class ColorCurve {
public:
    // t wrapped into [0, 1); keys kept sorted; at most 16 (later ones ignored).
    void add(float t, Color c);
    // Lerps between the keys around t, wrapping from the last key to the first. Empty -> kWhite.
    Color sample(float t) const;
    int size() const;
};
```

```cpp

#endif
```

### lam/math/dir4.h

```cpp
#include <lam/math/dir4.h>
```

Source: [`src/math/include/lam/math/dir4.h`](../src/math/include/lam/math/dir4.h). Namespaces: `lam`.

Four-way facing for top-down games (+y down). Enumerator order matches the row order of four-direction sprite sheets.

```cpp
hero.facing = dir4_of(input.move, hero.facing);
IVec2 ahead = cell + dir4_offset(hero.facing);
```

#### enum `Dir4`

```cpp
enum class Dir4 : std::uint8_t { Down, Left, Right, Up };
```

```cpp
constexpr Dir4 dir4_of(Vec2 v, Dir4 current);
```

The dominant axis of v. Ties, tiny and non-finite vectors keep `current`, so facing doesn't flicker on diagonals or when the stick is released.

```cpp
constexpr IVec2 dir4_offset(Dir4 d);
```

Down {0, 1}, Left {-1, 0}, Right {1, 0}, Up {0, -1} (+y is down).

```cpp
constexpr Vec2 dir4_vector(Dir4 d);
```

dir4_offset as a unit Vec2.

```cpp
constexpr Dir4 dir4_opposite(Dir4 d);
```

The opposite direction (Down <-> Up, Left <-> Right).

#### struct `SegmentHit`

First contact along a segment: t in [0, 1] of a->b, the point and the surface normal there. A segment starting inside reports t = 0 and a zero normal.

```cpp
struct SegmentHit {
    float t = 0;
    Vec2 point;
    Vec2 normal;
};
```

```cpp
std::optional<SegmentHit> intersect(const Segment &s, const Rect &r);
std::optional<SegmentHit> intersect(const Segment &s, const Circle &c);
```

```cpp
std::optional<SegmentHit> sweep_circle_rect(Vec2 from, Vec2 to, float radius, const Rect &r);
```

A circle of `radius` moving from -> to against a rectangle: first contact of its centre path.

### lam/math/grid.h

```cpp
#include <lam/math/grid.h>
```

Source: [`src/math/include/lam/math/grid.h`](../src/math/include/lam/math/grid.h). Namespaces: `lam`.

Row-major 2D grid for collision, costs, FOV and tiles. (0, 0) is the top-left; negative sizes clamp to 0.

#### class `Grid`

```cpp
template <class T> class Grid {
public:
    Grid() = default;
    Grid(int width, int height, T fill = T{});
    // Allocates; load time only.
    void resize(int width, int height, T fill = T{});
    int width() const;
    int height() const;
    std::size_t size() const;
    bool inside(int x, int y) const;
    bool inside(IVec2 p) const;
    // LAM_ASSERT(inside).
    std::size_t index(int x, int y) const;
    IVec2 coord(std::size_t i) const;
    T &operator()(int x, int y);
    const T &operator()(int x, int y) const;
    // The cell, or `outside` beyond the edges.
    T get_or(int x, int y, T outside) const;
    T get_or(IVec2 p, T outside) const;
    // Ignored outside.
    void set(int x, int y, T v);
    void fill(T v);
    std::span<T> cells();
    std::span<const T> cells() const;
    bool operator==(const Grid &) const = default;
};
```

### lam/math/rng.h

```cpp
#include <lam/math/rng.h>
```

Source: [`src/math/include/lam/math/rng.h`](../src/math/include/lam/math/rng.h). Namespaces: `lam`.

PCG32 seeded through SplitMix64. Integer maths only, so a seed gives the same sequence everywhere. Give each system its own stream (World::rng) so one can't shift another's draws.

#### class `Rng`

```cpp
class Rng {
public:
    explicit constexpr Rng(std::uint64_t seed = 0);
    constexpr void reseed(std::uint64_t seed);
    constexpr std::uint32_t next_u32();
    // [0, bound), without modulo bias. bound 0 -> 0.
    constexpr std::uint32_t below(std::uint32_t bound);
    // [lo, hi], both inclusive; lo > hi -> lo. Exact for the full int range.
    constexpr int between(int lo, int hi);
    // [0, 1) with 24 bits of resolution.
    constexpr float unit();
    // [lo, hi); lo >= hi -> lo. Never returns hi, even after float rounding.
    constexpr float range(float lo, float hi);
    // true with probability p (p <= 0 never, p >= 1 always).
    constexpr bool chance(float p);
    // A random unit vector (det_sin/det_cos).
    Vec2 unit_vector();
    // Uniform point in a disc of `radius` around the origin.
    Vec2 in_disc(float radius);
    // Fisher-Yates shuffle.
    template <class T> void shuffle(std::span<T> items);
    // For snapshots and saves: restores the sequence exactly.
    constexpr std::uint64_t state() const;
    constexpr void set_state(std::uint64_t s);
};
```

```cpp
constexpr std::uint64_t derive_seed(std::uint64_t base, std::uint64_t stream);
```

An independent seed from a base seed (SplitMix64 finaliser); `stream` picks which one.

### lam/core/assert.h

```cpp
#include <lam/core/assert.h>
```

Source: [`src/core/include/lam/core/assert.h`](../src/core/include/lam/core/assert.h).

LAM_ASSERT (debug), LAM_CHECK (always), LAM_UNREACHABLE. LAM_ENABLE_ASSERTS is a PUBLIC definition on lam_math/lam_core, so every target agrees.

```cpp
LAM_ASSERT(cond, msg)  API misuse and invariants; compiled out in Release.
LAM_CHECK(cond, msg)   violations that would corrupt memory; always on; logs and aborts.
```

```cpp
#if defined(LAM_ENABLE_ASSERTS) && LAM_ENABLE_ASSERTS
#define LAM_ASSERT(cond, msg) /* ... */
#else
#define LAM_ASSERT(cond, msg) ((void)0)
#endif
```

```cpp
#define LAM_CHECK(cond, msg) /* ... */
#define LAM_UNREACHABLE() /* ... */
```

```cpp
class AssetResolver {
public:
    virtual ~AssetResolver() = default;
    // Starts (or finds) a load of `path` as asset type `type`, retained by the current scope.
    // Returns AssetId bits, 0 if no loader handles the type and extension.
    virtual std::uint64_t resolve(TypeId type, std::string_view path) = 0;
    // The asset's path, or the name a runtime asset was given (AssetServer::add); "" for an
    // unnamed runtime asset (saved as null) or an unknown id.
    virtual std::string_view path_of(TypeId type, std::uint64_t bits) const = 0;
    virtual Result<std::string> read_text(std::string_view path) const = 0;  // root-relative, sync
    virtual std::size_t pending() const = 0;                    // queued + loading + finalizing
};
```

Banked fixed-step clock. advance() never returns more than max_ticks_per_frame; excess banked time is dropped so a hitch is followed by at most that many ticks.


```cpp
class FixedClock {
public:
    explicit FixedClock(int ticks_per_second = 60, double max_frame_seconds = 0.25,
                        int max_ticks_per_frame = 4);
    // Banks frame_seconds (capped at max_frame_seconds) and returns the ticks to run now.
    // Non-finite or negative -> 0.
    int advance(double frame_seconds);
    // [0, 1): the share of a tick banked but not yet run.
    float alpha() const;
    // Forgets banked time.
    void reset();
    int ticks_per_second() const;
    float tick_seconds() const;
};
```

### lam/core/data.h

```cpp
#include <lam/core/data.h>
```

Source: [`src/core/include/lam/core/data.h`](../src/core/include/lam/core/data.h). Namespaces: `lam`.

Strict JSON reading and canonical writing. nlohmann is private to data.cpp. Unread keys are errors unless ignored; every object handed out is checked by finish(); errors are sticky and name the file and JSON path; no exception leaves.

```cpp
Result<Enemy> r = parse_data<Enemy>(text, "enemy.json", [](DataReader &in) {
    return Enemy{.hp = in.integer("hp", 1, 999), .speed = in.number_or("speed", 1, 0, 10)};
});
```

#### enum `DataType`

```cpp
enum class DataType : std::uint8_t { Missing, Null, Bool, Number, String, Array, Object };
```

#### class `DataDocument`

Owns parsed JSON. Move-only. Readers point into it and must not outlive it.

```cpp
class DataDocument {
public:
    // Fails on malformed JSON and on nesting deeper than kMaxDataDepth, which would blow the stack.
    static Result<DataDocument> parse(std::string_view text, std::string_view file_name);
    static constexpr int kMaxDataDepth = 256;
    // The root object (a non-object root makes every read fail).
    DataReader root();
    // The first error, or any unread key in any object handed out.
    Status finish();
    // The first error so far, if any (does not check unread keys).
    bool failed() const;
    ~DataDocument();
    DataDocument(DataDocument &&) noexcept;
    DataDocument &operator=(DataDocument &&) noexcept;
    struct Impl;                                                // opaque (data.cpp)
};
```

#### class `DataReader`

One JSON object. Every typed read marks its key as read; a failed read records a sticky error (with file and path) and returns a neutral value (0, "", {}), so build code needs no checks.

```cpp
class DataReader {
public:
    DataReader() = default;
    bool has(std::string_view key) const;
    DataType type(std::string_view key) const;
    float number(std::string_view key, float min, float max);   // finite, in range
    float number_or(std::string_view key, float fallback, float min, float max);
    int integer(std::string_view key, int min, int max);        // 3.0 ok, 3.5 error
    int integer_or(std::string_view key, int fallback, int min, int max);
    std::int64_t integer64(std::string_view key, std::int64_t min, std::int64_t max);
    std::uint64_t u64(std::string_view key);
    double number64(std::string_view key, double min, double max);  // finite, in range, full precision
    bool boolean(std::string_view key);
    bool boolean_or(std::string_view key, bool fallback);
    std::string string(std::string_view key);                   // non-empty, valid UTF-8
    std::string text(std::string_view key);                     // may be empty
    std::string text_or(std::string_view key, std::string_view fallback);
    StrId id(std::string_view key);                             // name (interned) or "#<16 hex>"
    Vec2 vec2(std::string_view key);                            // [x, y]
    IVec2 ivec2(std::string_view key);
    Color color(std::string_view key);                          // "#rrggbb[aa]" or [r, g, b(, a)]
    Rect rect(std::string_view key);                            // [x, y, w, h]
    IRect irect(std::string_view key);
    DataReader object(std::string_view key);
    DataArray array(std::string_view key);
    // For dictionary-shaped objects. Views into the document; allocates.
    std::vector<std::string_view> keys() const;                 // document order
    void ignore(std::string_view key);                          // mark read (foreign formats: Tiled)
    void ignore_unknown();                                      // mark every key of this object read
    const std::string &path() const;                            // "/terrains/grass"
    void fail(std::string_view message);                        // custom error at this path
    bool failed() const;
    bool valid() const;                                         // false after a failed object()/array()
};
```

```cpp
template <class T, class Build>
Result<T> parse_data(std::string_view text, std::string_view file_name, Build build);
```

parse + build + finish in one call; no exception leaves it. build: T(DataReader &root).

#### class `DataWriter`

Canonical JSON writer: insertion order, no NaN/inf, invalid UTF-8 -> Error.

```cpp
DataWriter w; w.begin_object().key("hp").value(3).end_object(); Result<std::string> s = w.finish();
```

```cpp
class DataWriter {
public:
    DataWriter();
    ~DataWriter();
    DataWriter(DataWriter &&) noexcept;
    DataWriter &operator=(DataWriter &&) noexcept;
    DataWriter &begin_object();
    DataWriter &end_object();
    DataWriter &begin_array();
    DataWriter &end_array();
    DataWriter &key(std::string_view k);
    DataWriter &value(bool v);
    template <class I> requires(std::is_integral_v<I> && !std::is_same_v<I, bool>)
    DataWriter &value(I v);
    DataWriter &value(double v);
    DataWriter &value(float v);
    DataWriter &value(const char *v);                           // string literals are strings, not bools
    DataWriter &value(std::string_view v);
    DataWriter &value(const std::string &v);
    DataWriter &value(StrId v);                                 // name, else "#<16 hex>"
    DataWriter &value(Vec2 v);
    DataWriter &value(IVec2 v);
    DataWriter &value(Rect v);
    DataWriter &value(IRect v);
    DataWriter &value(Color v);
    DataWriter &null();
    DataWriter &copy(DataReader &in, std::string_view key);     // copies key: value; marks it read
    DataWriter &copy_rest(DataReader &in);                      // copies every unread key (migrations)
    DataWriter &raw(std::string_view json);                     // a pre-validated JSON value (engine use)
    Result<std::string> finish(bool pretty = false);            // Error on unbalanced/invalid input
};
```

### lam/core/events.h

```cpp
#include <lam/core/events.h>
```

Source: [`src/core/include/lam/core/events.h`](../src/core/include/lam/core/events.h). Namespaces: `lam`.

Typed event channels: one EventBus per world plus one for the App. Events carry the bus's sequence number, and `Ctx::read<T>()` returns what arrived since the stage last ran.

#### enum `EventScope`

```cpp
enum class EventScope : std::uint8_t { World, App };
```

#### class `Events`

```cpp
template <class T> class Events final : public detail::EventChannelBase {
public:
    Events(std::uint32_t *sequence, std::size_t capacity);
    // Appends e with the next bus sequence number. No allocation below capacity().
    void emit(const T &e);
    // Events with from <= seq < to, in emission order.
    std::span<const T> window(std::uint32_t from_seq, std::uint32_t to_seq) const;
    // Everything retained (tests, tools).
    std::span<const T> all() const;
    std::size_t capacity() const;
    // Raises capacity() to at least `capacity` and reserves that much (never shrinks). Cold path:
    // allocates when it grows. App::reserve_event calls it on every bus holding the channel.
    void reserve(std::size_t capacity);
    std::size_t size() const override;
    void trim(std::uint32_t before) override;
};
```

#### class `EventBus`

```cpp
class EventBus {
public:
    EventBus();
    ~EventBus();
    EventBus(const EventBus &) = delete;
    EventBus &operator=(const EventBus &) = delete;
    // Registers channel T (idempotent; a second call keeps the first capacity).
    template <class T> Events<T> &add(std::size_t capacity = 256);
    // LAM_ASSERT registered.
    template <class T> Events<T> &get();
    template <class T> Events<T> *try_get();
    template <class T> const Events<T> *try_get() const;
    // The next sequence number.
    std::uint32_t sequence() const;
    // Engine: drops events with seq < before in every channel.
    void trim(std::uint32_t before);
    // Events currently retained in all channels.
    std::size_t retained() const;
};
```

Fixed-capacity UTF-8 string for HUD, UI and debug text without per-frame allocation. Assignments truncate at a UTF-8 boundary.

#### class `FixedString`

```cpp
template <std::size_t N> class FixedString {
public:
    constexpr FixedString() = default;
    FixedString(std::string_view s);
    FixedString(const char *s);
    // Exact match for literals: without it `s = "x";` is ambiguous with the converting constructors.
    FixedString &operator=(const char *s);
    // Truncates at a UTF-8 boundary.
    FixedString &operator=(std::string_view s);
    std::string_view view() const;
    const char *c_str() const;
    std::size_t size() const;
    static constexpr std::size_t capacity();
    bool empty() const;
    void clear();
    bool operator==(const FixedString &) const = default;       // tail bytes are kept zeroed
    // Engine use (format_to): raw buffer write followed by set_size.
    char *buffer();
    void set_size(std::size_t n);
};
```

```cpp
    template <class T> T *try_get();
```

```cpp
class SettingsStore {
public:
    void define_int(std::string_view key, int def, int min, int max);
    void define_float(std::string_view key, float def, float min, float max);
    void define_bool(std::string_view key, bool def);
    void define_string(std::string_view key, std::string_view def);

    bool get_bool(std::string_view key) const;

    void set_int(std::string_view key, int v);
    void set_float(std::string_view key, float v);
    void set_bool(std::string_view key, bool v);
    void set_string(std::string_view key, std::string_view v);

    // Forgiving: bad or missing values keep their defaults. A missing file is not an error.
    Status load(const std::string &path);
    // Atomic write (write_file_atomic). Unknown loaded keys are written back unchanged.
    Status save(const std::string &path) const;

};
```

## Module ecs

CMake target `lam_ecs`. 10 public headers.

### lam/ecs/commands.h

```cpp
#include <lam/ecs/commands.h>
```

Source: [`src/ecs/include/lam/ecs/commands.h`](../src/ecs/include/lam/ecs/commands.h). Namespaces: `lam`.

Deferred structural changes, applied by the App after every stage run in record order. Records sit in arena chunks that never move and only allocate once the reserve is used up. Records for stale entities are dropped.

#### class `Commands`

One per World. Safe to record into while iterating Views.

```cpp
class Commands {
public:
    // Reserves `arena_bytes` up front.
    Commands(World &world, std::size_t arena_bytes);
    // Pending commands are discarded, not applied.
    ~Commands();
    Commands(const Commands &) = delete;
    Commands &operator=(const Commands &) = delete;
    // The index is reserved now; the entity and its components appear at apply().
    Entity spawn();
    template <class T> void add(Entity e, T value);             // hooks fire at apply()
    template <class T> void remove(Entity e);
    void destroy(Entity e);                                     // cascades to descendants
    void teleport(Entity e, Vec2 position);
    // Records the prefab's components now, so a later add<T>() for the returned entity replaces
    // the prefab's whole T.
    Entity spawn_prefab(StrId prefab, Vec2 position);
    // Engine use. Runs every record in order, including ones added while applying.
    void apply();
    std::size_t pending() const;                                // records not yet applied
    std::size_t bytes_used() const;                             // arena bytes held by pending records
    World &world();                                             // the owning World
};
```

### lam/ecs/component.h

```cpp
#include <lam/ecs/component.h>
```

Source: [`src/ecs/include/lam/ecs/component.h`](../src/ecs/include/lam/ecs/component.h). Namespaces: `lam`.

Component reflection: one description per type drives prefabs, saves, snapshots, hashing and the inspector. Put LAM_REFLECT\* at global scope right after the type, with its qualified name. Reflected types register during static init. Ids are per process, so saves use names.

#### enum `FieldType`

Reflected field kinds. Integers are stored with their own width; Enum values are 0..n-1.

```cpp
enum class FieldType : std::uint8_t { Bool, I8, U8, I16, U16, I32, U32, I64, U64, F32, F64,
    Vec2, IVec2, Rect, IRect, Color, Entity, StrId, FixedString, Enum, Asset, Struct, Array };
```

```cpp
struct TypeLayout;
```

In JSON: Vec2 [x, y], Rect [x, y, w, h], Color `"#rrggbb[aa]"` or [r, g, b(, a)], StrId and Enum by name, Asset by path, Entity as [index, generation] in saves and child index k in prefabs. An Array may list fewer than N elements; the rest keep their values.

#### struct `FieldInfo`

One reflected field. Built once per type (first use, cold path); lives for the process.

```cpp
struct FieldInfo {
    std::string_view name;                                      // JSON key (the member name)
    FieldType type = FieldType::Bool;
    FieldType element = FieldType::Bool;                        // element type when type == Array
    std::uint32_t offset = 0;                                   // bytes from the start of the owner
    std::uint32_t size = 0;                                     // bytes of one element; FixedString<N>: N
    std::uint16_t count = 1;                                    // Array length (std::array<E, N>)
    const TypeLayout *nested = nullptr;                         // Struct, or Array of Struct
    std::span<const std::string_view> enum_names = {};          // Enum (values 0..n-1)
    TypeId asset_type = 0;                                      // Asset: T of AssetId<T>
};
```

#### struct `TypeLayout`

The reflected shape of a type: its name, sizeof and fields in declaration order.

```cpp
struct TypeLayout {
    std::string_view name;
    std::uint32_t size = 0;                                     // sizeof(T); 0 for tags
    std::span<const FieldInfo> fields;
};
```

#### enum `ComponentFlags`

Per-type behaviour flags.

```cpp
enum ComponentFlags : std::uint32_t {
    kSerialize = 1,                                             // saved by serialize_world, read by prefabs
    kSnapshot = 2,                                              // copied by snapshots (undo)
    kHash = 4,                                                  // in state_hash; requires kSerialize
    kTag = 8,                                                   // no data, no dense storage
    kDefaultFlags = kSerialize | kSnapshot | kHash,
};
```

#### struct `SerializeContext`

For reads/writes that touch assets or entities. Prefabs fill entity_remap so an Entity field written as k means entity_remap[k]; saves leave it empty.

```cpp
struct SerializeContext {
    AssetResolver *assets = nullptr;                            // AssetId fields as paths; null: none
    std::span<const Entity> entity_remap = {};
};
```

```cpp
using ComponentId = std::uint16_t;
```

Index of a registered type; 0-based, dense, process-local (not a handle).

```cpp
using ComponentHook = void (*)(World &, Entity, void *);
```

Hook signature. The pointer is the component in its pool; valid only during the call.

#### struct `ComponentInfo`

Everything the engine knows about a registered type. The address never changes.

```cpp
struct ComponentInfo {
    std::string_view name;                                      // stable; used in JSON and saves
    ComponentId id = 0;
    TypeId type = 0;
    std::uint32_t size = 0, align = 0, flags = 0;               // unreflected types: flags 0; empty types: size 0
    const TypeLayout *layout = nullptr;                         // null: custom ops or unreflected
    void (*construct)(void *dst) = nullptr;                     // value-initialise T in raw storage
    void (*copy)(void *dst, const void *src) = nullptr;         // copy-assign into a constructed T
    void (*move)(void *dst, void *src) = nullptr;               // move-construct into raw storage; src stays constructed
    void (*destroy)(void *p) = nullptr;                         // run ~T
    // Reads the fields of one JSON object into a constructed T (missing keys keep their values).
    Status (*read)(void *dst, DataReader &in, const SerializeContext &ctx) = nullptr;
    // Writes one complete JSON value (an object for reflected types).
    void (*write)(const void *src, DataWriter &out, const SerializeContext &ctx) = nullptr;
    void (*hash)(const void *src, Hasher &h) = nullptr;
    ComponentHook on_add = nullptr;                             // first insert only
    ComponentHook on_replace = nullptr;                         // add<T> on an entity that has T
    ComponentHook on_remove = nullptr;
};
```

#### class `ComponentRegistry`

Process-global table of registered types. Main thread only.

```cpp
class ComponentRegistry {
public:
    static ComponentRegistry &global();
    // id() and info() register T on first use.
    template <class T> ComponentId id();
    template <class T> const ComponentInfo &info();
    // Reflected types win over unreflected ones of the same name. Linear: load time only.
    const ComponentInfo *find(std::string_view name) const;
    // LAM_CHECK(id < size()).
    const ComponentInfo &at(ComponentId id) const;
    std::size_t size() const;
    // Installs hooks for T (null clears one). Call during plugin build(), before entities exist.
    template <class T>
    void set_hooks(ComponentHook on_add, ComponentHook on_replace, ComponentHook on_remove);
    // Type-erased set_hooks.
    void set_hooks(ComponentId id, ComponentHook on_add, ComponentHook on_replace,
                   ComponentHook on_remove);
    // Sets T's flags; unreflected types can only use kSnapshot and kTag. Call before any World
    // stores T.
    template <class T> ComponentId register_type(std::uint32_t flags);
    // True when T is trivially copyable (pools and snapshots memcpy it).
    bool trivially_copyable(ComponentId id) const;
};
```

### lam/ecs/entity.h


Source: [`src/ecs/include/lam/ecs/entity.h`](../src/ecs/include/lam/ecs/entity.h). Namespaces: `lam`.

Generational entity handle. Copying one never keeps the entity alive; once the slot is reused the old handle just stops being alive.

#### struct `Entity`

Generation 0 means null. A slot whose generation reaches UINT32_MAX is retired.

```cpp
struct Entity {
    std::uint32_t index = 0;                                    // slot in the entity table
    std::uint32_t generation = 0;                               // 0 = null
    static constexpr Entity null();
    // Neither of these says whether the entity is alive.
    constexpr bool is_null() const;
    constexpr explicit operator bool() const;
    constexpr bool operator==(const Entity &) const = default;
    // Stable 64-bit key for hashing, maps and logs.
    constexpr std::uint64_t bits() const;
};
```

### lam/ecs/prefab.h

```cpp
#include <lam/ecs/prefab.h>
```

Source: [`src/ecs/include/lam/ecs/prefab.h`](../src/ecs/include/lam/ecs/prefab.h). Namespaces: `lam`.

Prefabs, compiled from JSON at load so spawning just copies bytes. "extends" copies a base and overrides fields; an Entity field may be a child index (0 = root). Asset fields resolve at load, so load prefabs after DefaultPlugins. A failed load changes nothing.

```cpp
{"prefabs": {"goblin": {"extends": "enemy", "tags": ["Enemy"],
  "components": {"Transform": {}, "Animator": {"sheet": "goblin.json", "clip": "idle"}},
  "children": [{"prefab": "torch", "offset": [4, -6]}]}}}
```

#### class `PrefabLibrary`

App resource shared by every world. Load on the main thread; spawning is const and cheap.

```cpp
class PrefabLibrary {
public:
    PrefabLibrary();                                            // empty
    ~PrefabLibrary();
    PrefabLibrary(const PrefabLibrary &) = delete;
    PrefabLibrary &operator=(const PrefabLibrary &) = delete;
    // Reads through ctx.assets when set, else from disk.
    Status load(std::string_view path, const SerializeContext &ctx);
    // Same-named prefabs are replaced.
    Status load_text(std::string_view json_text, std::string_view file_name,
                     const SerializeContext &ctx);
    bool has(StrId name) const;                                 // O(1)
    // Spawns now (not while iterating) and returns the root. Null for an unknown name.
    Entity spawn(World &w, StrId name, Vec2 position) const;
    // Same, recorded through `c` for an entity from c.spawn().
    void spawn_into(Commands &c, Entity e, StrId name, Vec2 position) const;
    std::span<const StrId> names() const;                       // load order
    void clear();                                               // forget every prefab
};
```

```cpp

```

Source: [`src/ecs/include/lam/ecs/snapshot.h`](../src/ecs/include/lam/ecs/snapshot.h). Namespaces: `lam`.

Snapshots for undo, replay checks and saves. A snapshot keeps the exact ECS layout, so restore reproduces iteration order and future entity indices bit for bit.

#### enum `EntitySlotState`

State of one entity-table slot in a snapshot.

```cpp
enum class EntitySlotState : std::uint8_t { Free = 0, Alive = 1, Retired = 2 };
```

#### struct `RngStreamState`

One RNG stream: its id and PCG32 state.

```cpp
struct RngStreamState {
    StrId stream;
    std::uint64_t state = 0;
};
```

#### class `WorldSnapshot`

A copy of a World's simulation state (World::snapshot_into). Move-only.

```cpp
class WorldSnapshot {
public:
    WorldSnapshot();                                            // empty; allocates nothing
    ~WorldSnapshot();
    WorldSnapshot(WorldSnapshot &&) noexcept;
    WorldSnapshot &operator=(WorldSnapshot &&) noexcept;
    std::size_t bytes() const;                                  // payload bytes held (sizes, not capacities)
    std::uint64_t tick() const;                                 // world tick when taken
    bool empty() const;                                         // never filled
    std::uint64_t seed() const;
    std::span<const std::uint32_t> generations() const;         // per entity index
    std::span<const EntitySlotState> slot_states() const;       // per entity index
    std::span<const std::uint32_t> free_list() const;           // back() is reused first
    std::span<const RngStreamState> rng_streams() const;        // creation order
    std::size_t pool_count() const;                             // pools, ascending ComponentId
    ComponentId pool_component(std::size_t i) const;
    std::span<const Entity> pool_entities(std::size_t i) const;  // dense order
    // pool_entities(i).size() constructed values with stride ComponentInfo::size; null for tags.
    const void *pool_data(std::size_t i) const;
    std::size_t resource_count() const;
    ComponentId resource_component(std::size_t i) const;        // registry entry of the resource type
    std::uint32_t resource_flags(std::size_t i) const;          // flags given to snapshot_resource
    const void *resource_data(std::size_t i) const;             // a constructed value
    // Empties the snapshot (keeps buffers) and sets its tick and seed.
    void reset(std::uint64_t tick, std::uint64_t seed);
    void set_entities(std::span<const std::uint32_t> generations,
                      std::span<const EntitySlotState> states,
                      std::span<const std::uint32_t> free_list);
    void set_rng_streams(std::span<const RngStreamState> streams);  // <= World::kMaxRngStreams
    // Pools must be added in ascending id order. Returns default-constructed values to fill.
    void *add_pool(ComponentId id, std::span<const Entity> entities);
    // Returns a default-constructed value to fill.
    void *add_resource(ComponentId id, std::uint32_t flags);
    // Consistency check for a hand-built snapshot. Run before World::restore.
    Status validate() const;
};
```

#### class `History`

Undo/redo for puzzle and editor-style games; no allocation after warm-up. Undo rewinds the whole world, presentation included, so handles taken after a push may point at a different entity.

```cpp
class History {
public:
    // Limits cover undo and redo together. The newest undo entry is always kept.
    explicit History(std::size_t max_bytes = 64u << 20, std::size_t max_entries = 256);
    ~History();
    History(const History &) = delete;
    History &operator=(const History &) = delete;
    void push(const World &w);                                  // clears redo; evicts oldest past limits
    // False if there's nothing to undo or redo.
    bool undo(World &w, RestoreOptions o = {.tick = false});
    bool redo(World &w, RestoreOptions o = {.tick = false});
    bool can_undo() const;
    bool can_redo() const;
    void clear();                                               // drops every entry and frees buffers
    std::size_t size() const;                                   // stored snapshots (undo + redo)
    std::size_t bytes() const;                                  // sum of stored WorldSnapshot::bytes()
};
```

### lam/ecs/world.h

```cpp
#include <lam/ecs/world.h>
```

Source: [`src/ecs/include/lam/ecs/world.h`](../src/ecs/include/lam/ecs/world.h). Namespaces: `lam`.

The ECS world: sparse-set pools, world resources and events, per-world RNG streams. Iteration order depends only on the sequence of structural changes, so it's deterministic. Changing a pool while a View iterates it fails LAM_CHECK in every build.

#### struct `With`

```cpp
template <class... W> struct With {};                           // required tags/components, not yielded
```

#### struct `Exclude`

```cpp
template <class... X> struct Exclude {};                        // entities with any X are skipped
```

#### class `View`

Entities with every T. While iterating, the pools are locked: use world.commands() for structural changes. Tags yield a shared dummy reference; `With<Tag>` filters without one.

```cpp
for (auto [e, t] : w.view<Transform>()) ...
```

```cpp
template <class... T> class View {                              // drives from the smallest pool, dense order
public:
    static constexpr std::size_t kMaxFilters = 8;               // With<> and Exclude<> types
    class Iterator;                                             // yields std::tuple<Entity, T&...>
    // Locks the pools and returns the first match.
    Iterator begin();
    Iterator end();
    // Fastest way to iterate.
    template <class F> void each(F &&f);                        // f(Entity, T&...)
    std::size_t size_hint() const;                              // upper bound on matches
    ~View();
    View(const View &) = delete;
    View &operator=(const View &) = delete;
    View(View &&o) noexcept;                                    // takes over the lock
    View &operator=(View &&) = delete;
};
```

#### class `View<T...>::Iterator`

Forward iterator over a View's matches; valid while its View is alive.

```cpp
template <class... T> class View<T...>::Iterator {
public:
    using value_type = std::tuple<Entity, T &...>;
    using difference_type = std::ptrdiff_t;
    Iterator() = default;
    value_type operator*() const;
    Iterator &operator++();
    bool operator==(const Iterator &o) const;
};
```

App::create_world fills this from AppConfig.

```cpp
struct WorldConfig {
    std::size_t entity_capacity = 16384;                        // entity table pre-size (no-alloc below it)
    std::uint64_t seed = 1;                                     // base of every RNG stream
    std::size_t commands_arena_bytes = 256 * 1024;              // Commands pre-reserved bytes
    StrId name;
};
```

What World::restore puts back besides entities, components and resources.

```cpp
struct RestoreOptions {
    bool tick = true;                                           // false: keep the current tick (undo)
    bool rng = true;                                            // false: keep the current RNG streams and seed
};
```

#### struct `WorldRestored`

```cpp
struct WorldRestored {                                          // World event after restore/deserialize
    std::uint64_t tick = 0;
};
```

#### class `World`

Main thread only. Component hooks fire on add, remove and destroy, never on restore or when the World itself is destroyed. Not movable.

```cpp
class World {
public:
    static constexpr std::uint32_t kMaxRngStreams = 32;
    explicit World(WorldConfig config = {});
    ~World();
    World(const World &) = delete;
    World &operator=(const World &) = delete;
    std::uint32_t id() const;                                   // unique per process, never reused, != 0
    StrId name() const;
    // Entities
    Entity create();                                            // O(1); reuses freed index with gen+1
    void destroy(Entity e);                                     // immediate; cascades to Children; LAM_CHECK(!iterating())
    bool alive(Entity e) const;                                 // false for null and stale handles
    std::size_t entity_count() const;                           // pending spawns not included
    // Components. References stay valid until pool T changes structurally.
    // Assigns if e already has T (on_replace), else constructs it (on_add).
    template <class T, class... A> T &add(Entity e, A &&...args);
    template <class T> void remove(Entity e);                   // on_remove; no-op if absent
    template <class T> bool has(Entity e) const;
    template <class T> T &get(Entity e);                        // LAM_ASSERT has
    template <class T> const T &get(Entity e) const;
    template <class T> T *try_get(Entity e);                    // null if absent, dead or stale
    template <class T> const T *try_get(Entity e) const;
    template <class... T> View<T...> view();
    template <class... T, class... X> View<T...> view(Exclude<X...>);
    template <class... T, class... W, class... X> View<T...> view(With<W...>, Exclude<X...> = {});
    template <class T> Entity single();                         // LAM_ASSERT exactly one entity has T
    // Null if none; asserts there's at most one.
    template <class T> T *single_or_null(Entity *out = nullptr);
    template <class T> std::size_t count() const;
    template <class T> void reserve(std::size_t n);             // pre-size (no-alloc guarantee)
    template <class T> std::uint32_t pool_version() const;      // ++ on every structural change of pool T
    // Moves the entities each Follow pool shares with Lead to the front, in Lead's order.
    template <class Lead, class... Follow> void align();
    // Stable. less(const T&, const T&), or less(Entity, Entity) for tags.
    template <class T, class Less> void sort(Less less);
    void teleport(Entity e, Vec2 position);                     // Transform + PrevTransform; subtree JustSpawned
    // Type-erased access (serialisation, prefabs, inspector)
    void *get_raw(Entity e, ComponentId id);                    // null if absent; empty types: a dummy
    void *add_raw(Entity e, ComponentId id, bool fire_hooks = true);  // default-constructed
    void remove_raw(Entity e, ComponentId id);                  // on_remove; no-op if absent
    // Fills `out` with e's component ids in ascending order; returns the total count.
    std::size_t components_of(Entity e, std::span<ComponentId> out) const;
    // Resources, events, commands, prefabs
    Resources &resources();
    const Resources &resources() const;
    EventBus &events();
    Commands &commands();                                       // applied by the App after each stage
    // Includes resource T in snapshots, saves and the hash. kSerialize and kHash need reflection.
    template <class T> void snapshot_resource(std::uint32_t flags = kSnapshot | kHash | kSerialize);
    // Run after restore/deserialize to rebuild derived state. Adding a hook twice runs it twice,
    // so add them in Plugin::init_world or check has_restore_hook first.
    void add_restore_hook(void (*hook)(World &));
    bool has_restore_hook(void (*hook)(World &)) const;
    void set_prefabs(const PrefabLibrary *prefabs);             // set by App for every world
    const PrefabLibrary *prefabs() const;                       // null until set
    // Determinism
    Rng &rng(StrId stream);                                     // created on first use, at most kMaxRngStreams
    void reseed(std::uint64_t seed);                            // every stream re-derived
    std::uint64_t seed() const;
    std::uint64_t tick() const;                                 // ticks this world has run
    void advance_tick();                                        // engine
    // Copies the entity table, RNG state and every kSnapshot/kSerialize pool and resource.
    void snapshot_into(WorldSnapshot &out) const;               // reuses buffers: no alloc after warm-up
    // Puts the snapshot back exactly and discards pending commands. Component hooks don't fire;
    // restore hooks do. Validate hand-built snapshots first.
    void restore(const WorldSnapshot &s, RestoreOptions o = {});
    // Hash of the tick, RNG states, live entities and kHash pools and resources. Frame stages must
    // not create or destroy entities in a ticking world, or replays will diverge.
    std::uint64_t state_hash() const;
    // Destroys every entity (hooks fire) and resets the free list, so indices restart from 0.
    void clear();                                               // keeps resources
    bool iterating() const;                                     // a View holds the pools locked
};
```

## Module app

CMake target `lam_app`. 2 public headers.

### lam/core/app.h

```cpp
#include <lam/core/app.h>
```

Source: [`src/core/app/include/lam/core/app.h`](../src/core/app/include/lam/core/app.h). Namespaces: `lam`.

App: worlds, the stage loop, plugins, resources and events. Systems are plain function pointers and all state lives in resources and components. Main thread only; the frame path doesn't allocate in steady state.

```cpp
App app({.title = "Hop"}, argc, argv);
app.add_plugins(DefaultPlugins{});
app.add_system(Stage::Simulate, move_things, "game.move");
return app.run();
```

#### enum `Stage`

The twelve fixed stages, in frame order. TickBegin..TickEnd run once per fixed tick.

```cpp
enum class Stage : std::uint8_t { FrameBegin, TickBegin, Input, Simulate, Physics, PostPhysics,
    Animate, TickEnd, Update, Render, RenderUI, FrameEnd, Count };
```

```cpp
std::string_view stage_name(Stage s);
```

"FrameBegin", "TickBegin", ...; "?" for Count. Static storage.

```cpp
constexpr bool is_tick_stage(Stage s);
```

True for TickBegin..TickEnd (the stages that run once per fixed tick).

#### enum `SystemScope`

PerWorld runs on every world in the stack taking part in the stage, menus and overlays too, so gate game rules with run_if or only_world. Once runs on the focused world (or main).

```cpp
enum class SystemScope : std::uint8_t { PerWorld, Once };
```

```cpp
inline constexpr int kMaxWorlds = 8;
```

Maximum entries in the world stack (App::set_world_stack).

#### class `Ctx`

Handed to every system. Cheap to copy; valid only during the call.

```cpp
class Ctx {
public:
    App &app() const;
    World &world() const;                                       // PerWorld: that world; Once: focused or main
    Commands &commands() const;                                 // world().commands()
    const Time &time() const;                                   // per world (time.h)
    bool focused() const;                                       // this world receives input
    Stage stage() const;
    SystemScope scope() const;
    // App resource; a missing one aborts with a message naming the fix.
    template <class T> T &res() const;
    template <class T> T *try_res() const;                      // null if absent
    // World resource of ctx.world(); aborts the same way if missing.
    template <class T> T &local() const;
    template <class T> T *try_local() const;                    // null if absent
    // Appends to the world or App channel T was registered on. Aborts if T isn't registered:
    // register it in your own build() too (add_event is idempotent) or use try_emit.
    template <class T> void emit(const T &e) const;
    // T events emitted since this stage last ran here, each seen once. Events emitted earlier in
    // the same stage pass show up on the next run. Valid until the system returns.
    template <class T> std::span<const T> read() const;
    template <class T> bool has_event() const;                  // registered in either scope
    // emit() if T is registered; returns whether it did. For events of optional plugins.
    template <class T> bool try_emit(const T &e) const;
    // Per-world stream, snapshotted and hashed. Tick stages and startup only; code without a Ctx
    // uses world.rng(stream) directly.
    Rng &rng(StrId stream) const;
    Rng &fx_rng() const;                                        // presentation only; never hashed or replayed
};
```

```cpp
template <class T> bool has_local(const Ctx &ctx);
```

run_if predicate: true when ctx.world() holds the World resource T.

```cpp
using SystemFn = void (*)(Ctx &);
```

```cpp
using RunIf = bool (*)(const Ctx &);
```

Checked before each call; false skips that call only. Engine systems keep running, so to freeze a world stop its ticks (a blocking Scene, WorldEntry::ticks or App::set_paused).

#### struct `SystemDesc`

Everything add_system needs. Allowed scopes: Input..Animate PerWorld only, FrameEnd Once only (LAM_CHECK). Order within a pass is (order, registration index).

```cpp
struct SystemDesc {
    Stage stage = Stage::Simulate;
    SystemFn fn = nullptr;
    std::string_view name;                                      // static storage; unique per (stage, only_world)
    // Engine orders are in docs/GUIDE.md. Game systems use (-1000, 1000), which in Animate is after
    // the animators: set clips in PostPhysics, override what the animators wrote in Animate.
    int order = 0;
    SystemScope scope = SystemScope::PerWorld;
    RunIf run_if = nullptr;                                     // null = always
    std::uint32_t only_world = 0;                               // World::id(); 0 = every world
};
```

#### class `Plugin`

Plugins build in the order they're added and init_world runs on every world, existing or later. finish runs at run(); shutdown_world/shutdown go in reverse build order.

```cpp
class Plugin {
public:
    virtual ~Plugin() = default;
    virtual std::string_view name() const = 0;                  // unique, e.g. "lam.physics"
    virtual void build(App &app) = 0;                           // components, App resources, events, systems, loaders
    virtual void init_world(App &app, World &world);            // world resources
    virtual void finish(App &app);                              // after every plugin built
    virtual void shutdown_world(App &app, World &world);
    virtual void shutdown(App &app);                            // reverse order
};
```

#### struct `AppConfig`

Startup configuration. Designated initialisers must follow declaration order.

```cpp
struct AppConfig {
    std::string title = "LambdaEngine2D";
    IVec2 window_size{1280, 720};                               // points
    IVec2 virtual_size{480, 270};                               // pixel-art target
    int tick_rate = 60;                                         // fixed ticks per second
    double max_frame_seconds = 0.25;                            // longer frames are capped
    int max_ticks_per_frame = 4;                                // also sizes event channels
    std::uint64_t seed = 1;                                     // every world seed derives from it
    bool resizable = true;
    bool vsync = true;
    bool audio = true;                                          // false: no audio device, sound is silent
    bool wait_for_startup_assets = true;
    std::size_t entity_capacity = 16384;                        // per world (WorldConfig)
    std::string settings_file = "settings.json";                // in user_data_dir(title); "" = none
};
```

#### struct `LaunchOptions`

Command-line flags. Unknown ones are kept in `extra`.

```cpp
struct LaunchOptions {
    bool hidden = false;                                        // --hidden (not vsync-paced; pair with --step)
    bool headless = false;                                      // --headless: NullPlatform, no backends
    bool step = false;                                          // --step: one tick per frame, frame_dt = tick_dt
    int frames = 0;                                             // --frames N: quit after N frames
    int draw_every = 1;                                         // --draw-every N (FrameEnd still swaps)
    std::uint64_t seed = 0;                                     // --seed S (0 = AppConfig::seed)
    std::string record_input;                                   // --record-input FILE
    std::string replay;                                         // --replay FILE
    bool replay_any_build = false;                              // --replay-any-build
    std::string screenshot;                                     // --screenshot FILE (last frame)
    int hash_every = 0;                                         // --hash-every N
    bool print_schedule = false;                                // --print-schedule: log system order, exit
    bool no_vsync = false;                                      // --no-vsync (benches)
    std::vector<std::string> extra;                             // unknown arguments, in order
    // True if `flag` is in `extra`, or is a known boolean flag that is set ("--headless").
    bool has(std::string_view flag) const;
    // Game flags: "--enemies 2000" or "--enemies=2000" -> "2000". nullopt if absent or last.
    std::optional<std::string_view> value(std::string_view flag) const;
    // value(flag) as a decimal int; `fallback` if absent or not a whole number in int range.
    int int_value(std::string_view flag, int fallback) const;
    bool deterministic() const;                                 // headless || step || record || replay
    // deterministic(), --hidden, --frames or --bot. Scripted runs leave the settings file and the
    // data dir alone.
    bool scripted() const;
};
```

```cpp
LaunchOptions parse_launch_options(int argc, const char *const *argv);
```

Parses argv[1..argc). A value flag without a valid value is kept in `extra`; --seed also takes 0x-hex. argv may be null when argc is 0.

#### struct `WorldEntry`

One world in the frame's stack (bottom first). The world must belong to this App.

```cpp
struct WorldEntry {
    World *world = nullptr;
    bool ticks = true;                                          // runs tick stages
    bool visible = true;                                        // runs Update/Render/RenderUI
    bool input = true;                                          // Ctx::focused() (topmost input world wins)
};
```

#### class `App`

```cpp
class App {
public:
    // Parses argv, inserts SettingsStore, PrefabLibrary, Profiler and DebugOverlay, registers the
    // engine components, events and systems, and creates the main world.
    explicit App(AppConfig config = {}, int argc = 0, const char *const *argv = nullptr);
    // Shuts plugins down in reverse build order, then destroys worlds, resources and plugins.
    ~App();
    App(const App &) = delete;
    App &operator=(const App &) = delete;
    // Builds the plugin now and runs init_world on existing worlds. Names must be unique.
    template <class P, class... A> P &add_plugin(A &&...args);
    template <class Bundle> App &add_plugins(const Bundle &bundle);  // bundle.build(*this)
    // True once a plugin with that name was added (also while its build() runs).
    bool has_plugin(std::string_view name) const;
    // run() aborts, naming both plugins, if `needed` was never added.
    void require_plugin(std::string_view needed, std::string_view by);
    // Systems (changes during a pass are queued)
    App &add_system(Stage stage, SystemFn fn, std::string_view name, int order = 0);
    App &add_system(const SystemDesc &desc);
    // Runs once on the main world before frame 1 (or the next frame, if added later). Commands
    // are applied after each one; rng() is allowed.
    App &add_startup(SystemFn fn, std::string_view name);
    // Removes every system whose only_world == world_id (queued during a pass).
    void remove_systems_of(std::uint32_t world_id);
    // Adds a TickEnd +1100 system that keeps the Follow pools in Lead's dense order. Idempotent.
    template <class Lead, class... Follow> App &align_pools();
    // One line per system in run order, for --print-schedule.
    std::string schedule_text() const;
    // Data
    // Only needed for unreflected types; reflected ones register during static init.
    template <class T> App &register_component();
    // Registers channel T on every world or on the App bus, reserving capacity x
    // (max_ticks_per_frame + 1). Repeat calls keep the first capacity. Full channels grow.
    template <class T>
    App &add_event(EventScope scope = EventScope::World, std::size_t capacity = 256);
    // Raises T's reserve to at least capacity x (max_ticks_per_frame + 1). Never shrinks.
    template <class T> App &reserve_event(std::size_t capacity);
    // True once add_event<T> was called (either scope).
    template <class T> bool has_event() const;
    // App resource, constructed in place; LAM_ASSERT absent.
    template <class T, class... A> T &insert_resource(A &&...args);
    template <class T> T &res();                                // App resource; aborts if absent
    template <class T> T *try_res();                            // null if absent
    Resources &resources();                                     // App resources
    EventBus &events();                                         // App-scope events
    // Worlds
    World &main_world();                                        // from construction; never destroyed
    // New world seeded from seed() and its name; every plugin's init_world runs on it.
    World &create_world(std::string_view name);
    void destroy_world(World &w);                               // queued if a pass is running
    // First live world with this name (scene worlds use Scene::name()), or null. Still works after
    // run() returns, which headless summaries rely on.
    World *find_world(StrId name);
    // Bottom first, at most kMaxWorlds; empty means {main_world}. Picked up after the FrameBegin
    // and TickBegin Once passes.
    void set_world_stack(std::span<const WorldEntry> entries);
    // The stack the loop is running on; {main_world} before the first frame.
    std::span<const WorldEntry> world_stack() const;
    // Topmost world of the active stack with input == true; null if none.
    World *focused_world() const;
    // Services
    void set_platform(std::unique_ptr<Platform> platform);      // default: NullPlatform
    Platform &platform();                                       // valid until set_platform
    void set_asset_resolver(AssetResolver *resolver);           // AssetsPlugin
    AssetResolver *asset_resolver() const;                      // null until AssetsPlugin
    SerializeContext serialize_context() const;                 // {asset_resolver(), {}}
    const AppConfig &config() const;                            // as given (sanitised)
    const LaunchOptions &options() const;                       // parsed from argv
    // Per-user data folder, created on call. Empty in scripted runs unless LAM_DATA_DIR is set, so
    // put saves here and bots and tests won't touch the player's.
    std::string data_dir() const;
    void set_seed(std::uint64_t seed);                          // until run(); reseeds every world
    std::uint64_t seed() const;                                 // --seed or AppConfig::seed
    std::uint64_t tick() const;                                 // app tick
    const Time &time() const;                                   // tick == app_tick
    Rng &fx_rng();                                              // presentation only; never hashed
    // Holds ticks and resets the fixed clock. InputPlugin watches paused() to reset its latch.
    void set_paused(bool paused);
    bool paused() const;
    // Running
    // Runs finish, startup and the loop until quit; returns the exit code. Nothing is destroyed
    // until ~App, so state can still be read afterwards.
    int run();
    void run_frames(int frames);                                // tests: exact number of frames
    // For tests: `ticks` frames of one tick each, unless ticks are held (paused, startup assets).
    void step_ticks(int ticks);
    // Stops run() after the current frame and saves settings (not in headless).
    void quit(int exit_code = 0);
    bool quitting() const;                                      // quit() was called
};
```

#### class `Platform`

Owned by the App (App::set_platform). Main thread only.

```cpp
class Platform {
public:
    virtual ~Platform() = default;
    // The user asked to close the window; run() quits.
    virtual bool should_close() = 0;
    // Monotonic seconds from an arbitrary origin.
    virtual double now_seconds() = 0;
    // FrameBegin -10000: poll events, start drawing.
    virtual void begin_frame() = 0;
    // FrameEnd +10000: swap and poll. Runs every frame, even with --draw-every.
    virtual void end_frame() = 0;
    virtual WindowInfo window() const = 0;
    virtual void set_fullscreen(bool on) = 0;                   // borderless
    virtual bool has_gpu() const = 0;
};
```

#### class `NullPlatform`

Headless: the clock advances exactly 1/tick_rate per begin_frame(). Never closes, no GPU.

```cpp
class NullPlatform final : public Platform {
public:
    // framebuffer is also reported as the window size and safe area, at dpi 1.
    explicit NullPlatform(int tick_rate = 60, IVec2 framebuffer = {640, 360});
    bool should_close() override;
    double now_seconds() override;
    void begin_frame() override;
    void end_frame() override;
    WindowInfo window() const override;
    void set_fullscreen(bool on) override;                      // only records the flag
    bool has_gpu() const override;
};
```

### lam/assets/asset_server.h

```cpp
#include <lam/assets/asset_server.h>
```

Source: [`src/assets/include/lam/assets/asset_server.h`](../src/assets/include/lam/assets/asset_server.h). Namespaces: `lam`.

Typed asset server: loads cached by path and held by scopes, one IO/decode worker, main-thread finalize in load order, hot reload in LAM_DEV builds. Main thread only, except LoadContext.

```cpp
using AssetScope = std::uint32_t;
inline constexpr AssetScope kRootScope = 0;
```

#### class `LoadContext`

Passed to decode(), possibly on the worker; don't touch the server or the App from there. Paths inside an asset file are relative to that file; paths in code are relative to the root.

```cpp
class LoadContext {
public:
    // Made by the server for each decode; parent_* identify the asset being decoded.
    LoadContext(AssetServer &server, std::string_view path, std::uint64_t parent_bits,
                TypeId parent_type);
    std::string_view path() const;                              // root-relative
    Result<std::vector<std::byte>> read(std::string_view relative_path) const;  // next to path()
    // Queues a dependency next to path(). The parent retains it and finalizes after it is Ready;
    // if it fails, the parent fails.
    template <class U> AssetId<U> depend(std::string_view relative_path);
};
```

#### struct `FinalizeContext`

Passed to finalize()/unload() on the main thread. What finalize() adds or loads into the current scope belongs to the asset being finalized; pass kRootScope to outlive it.

```cpp
struct FinalizeContext {
    App &app;
    AssetServer &server;
    std::string_view path;
};
```

#### class `AssetLoaderBase`

```cpp
class AssetLoaderBase {
public:
    virtual ~AssetLoaderBase() = default;
    // Lower-case extensions with the dot, matched against the file name's suffix, longest first
    // (".sounds.json" before ".json"). Return a span over static storage.
    virtual std::span<const std::string_view> extensions() const = 0;
    virtual TypeId type() const = 0;                            // type_id<T>() of the asset type
    // Type-erased forms of AssetLoader<T>; implemented there (final).
    virtual Result<void *> decode_erased(std::span<const std::byte> bytes, LoadContext &ctx) = 0;
    virtual Status finalize_erased(void *asset, FinalizeContext &ctx) = 0;
    virtual void unload_erased(void *asset, FinalizeContext &ctx) = 0;
    virtual void destroy_erased(void *asset) = 0;
};
```

#### class `AssetLoader`

```cpp
template <class T> class AssetLoader : public AssetLoaderBase {
public:
    virtual Result<T> decode(std::span<const std::byte> bytes, LoadContext &ctx) = 0;  // CPU only
    // Main thread, every dependency Ready (GPU uploads, atlas packing). An error fails the asset.
    virtual Status finalize(T &asset, FinalizeContext &ctx);
    // Main thread, before the value is destroyed (GC, reload swap, shutdown).
    virtual void unload(T &asset, FinalizeContext &ctx);
    TypeId type() const final;
    Result<void *> decode_erased(std::span<const std::byte> bytes, LoadContext &ctx) final;
    Status finalize_erased(void *asset, FinalizeContext &ctx) final;
    void unload_erased(void *asset, FinalizeContext &ctx) final;
    void destroy_erased(void *asset) final;
};
```

#### struct `AssetEvent`

```cpp
template <class T> struct AssetEvent {                          // App event; registered on first use of T
    // Loaded: Ready (first time, or after Failed); Failed; Modified: reloaded or mark_modified;
    // Removed: unloaded (the id is dead).
    enum class Kind : std::uint8_t { Loaded, Failed, Modified, Removed };
    Kind kind = Kind::Loaded;
    AssetId<T> id;
};
```

```cpp
    float watch_interval_seconds = 0.5f;                        // hot reload: poll period per file

};
```

#### class `AssetServer`

```cpp
class AssetServer final : public AssetResolver {                // App resource (AssetsPlugin)
public:
    AssetServer(App &app, AssetsConfig config);                 // resolves the root, starts the worker
    ~AssetServer() override;                                    // no unload callbacks run here
    AssetServer(const AssetServer &) = delete;
    AssetServer &operator=(const AssetServer &) = delete;
    // Registers `loader` for (T, each of its extensions); the last registration wins.
    template <class T> void register_loader(std::unique_ptr<AssetLoader<T>> loader);
    // Starts (or finds, cached by type + path) a load retained by the current scope. Returns at
    // once; state() becomes Ready after finalize (immediately in synchronous mode).
    template <class T> AssetId<T> load(std::string_view path);
    template <class T> AssetId<T> load(std::string_view path, AssetScope scope);
    // Loads synchronously (decode + dependencies + finalize). Startup and tests.
    template <class T> Result<AssetId<T>> load_now(std::string_view path);
    template <class T> Result<AssetId<T>> load_now(std::string_view path, AssetScope scope);
    template <class T> Handle<T> load_handle(std::string_view path);  // explicit refcount (rare)
    // Runtime-made asset, Ready at once. A non-empty `name` lets load<T>(name), prefabs and saves
    // find it while it lives, so add it before loading prefabs that use it.
    template <class T> AssetId<T> add(T value, std::string_view name = {});
    template <class T> AssetId<T> add(T value, std::string_view name, AssetScope scope);
    // Null unless Ready. The pointer is valid until the end of the current stage.
    template <class T> const T *get(AssetId<T> id) const;
    // Like get(); for in-place edits, followed by mark_modified(id).
    template <class T> T *get_mut(AssetId<T> id);
    // Call after editing a Ready asset through get_mut: bumps version() and emits Modified.
    template <class T> void mark_modified(AssetId<T> id);
    // None for null, stale or unloaded ids.
    template <class T> LoadState state(AssetId<T> id) const;
    // The error while Failed, else null.
    template <class T> const Error *error(AssetId<T> id) const;
    // The normalised path, or the add() name; "" for unnamed runtime assets and unknown ids.
    template <class T> std::string_view path_of(AssetId<T> id) const;
    template <class T> std::uint32_t version(AssetId<T> id) const;
    // Blocking reload: decode a new value, swap it in, reload dependants; on error the old value
    // stays. Busy while the first load is in flight, Unsupported for add()ed assets.
    template <class T> Status reload(AssetId<T> id);
    // Scopes
    AssetScope begin_scope();
    void end_scope(AssetScope scope);                           // releases its retains; GC at next update()
    // The scope that load(path) / add(value) without a scope retain into (kRootScope by default).
    void set_current_scope(AssetScope scope);
    AssetScope current_scope() const;
    bool all_ready() const;                                     // no load or reload in flight
    std::size_t pending() const override;                       // loads and reloads in flight
    // Loads held by `scope` (directly or as deps) that are neither Ready nor Failed. Reloads of
    // Ready assets don't count.
    std::size_t pending(AssetScope scope) const;
    void wait_all();                                            // main thread: until pending() == 0
    std::string resolve_path(std::string_view relative) const;  // absolute path under root()
    const std::string &root() const;                            // the resolved asset root
    bool synchronous() const;                                   // deterministic runs, AssetsConfig::synchronous
    void collect_garbage();                                     // unload assets nothing retains
    void update();                                              // engine: FrameBegin -3000
    // AssetResolver
    std::uint64_t resolve(TypeId type, std::string_view path) override;
    std::string_view path_of(TypeId type, std::uint64_t bits) const override;
    Result<std::string> read_text(std::string_view path) const override;
    // Type-erased core behind the templates above (implemented in src/assets); prefer those.
    using EmitFn = void (*)(App &app, std::uint8_t kind, std::uint64_t bits);
    using DestroyFn = void (*)(void *value);
    void register_type(TypeId type, EmitFn emit);               // idempotent
    void register_erased(std::unique_ptr<AssetLoaderBase> loader);
    std::uint64_t load_erased(TypeId type, std::string_view path, AssetScope scope);
    Result<std::uint64_t> load_now_erased(TypeId type, std::string_view path, AssetScope scope);
    std::uint64_t add_erased(TypeId type, void *value, DestroyFn destroy, std::string_view name,
                             AssetScope scope);
    const void *get_erased(TypeId type, std::uint64_t bits) const;
    void *get_mut_erased(TypeId type, std::uint64_t bits);
    void mark_modified_erased(TypeId type, std::uint64_t bits);
    LoadState state_erased(TypeId type, std::uint64_t bits) const;
    const Error *error_erased(TypeId type, std::uint64_t bits) const;
    std::uint32_t version_erased(TypeId type, std::uint64_t bits) const;
    Status reload_erased(TypeId type, std::uint64_t bits);
    void retain_erased(TypeId type, std::uint64_t bits);
    void release_erased(TypeId type, std::uint64_t bits);
};
```

#### class `Handle`

Explicit strong reference (main thread). Most code relies on scopes. The server must outlive it.

```cpp
template <class T> class Handle {
public:
    Handle() = default;
    Handle(AssetServer &server, AssetId<T> id);
    Handle(const Handle &o);
    Handle(Handle &&o) noexcept;
    Handle &operator=(const Handle &o);
    Handle &operator=(Handle &&o) noexcept;
    ~Handle();
    AssetId<T> id() const;
    explicit operator bool() const;
};
```

#### struct `TextAsset`

```cpp
struct TextAsset {                                              // ".txt", built-in loader
    std::string text;
};
```

#### class `AssetsPlugin`

```cpp
class AssetsPlugin final : public Plugin {
public:
    explicit AssetsPlugin(AssetsConfig c = {});
    std::string_view name() const override;
    // Inserts AssetServer, the TextAsset loader, asset_update (FrameBegin -3000) and, in sync
    // mode, asset_tick_collect (TickBegin -3000).
    void build(App &app) override;
    void shutdown(App &app) override;                           // unloads everything
};
```

CMake target `lam_render`. 15 public headers.

### lam/render/atlas.h

```cpp
#include <lam/render/atlas.h>
```

Source: [`src/render/include/lam/render/atlas.h`](../src/render/include/lam/render/atlas.h). Namespaces: `lam`.

Load-time atlases. Image loaders pack into named groups at finalize, in AssetId order so the layout is deterministic. Opt out with "atlas": "none". Pages are 2048x2048 and never shrink.

#### class `AtlasPacker`

```cpp
class AtlasPacker {                                             // shelf packer
public:
    explicit AtlasPacker(int page_size = 2048, int padding = 1,
                         IVec2 reserved = {kBuiltinImageSize, kBuiltinImageSize});
    struct Placement {
        int page = 0;
        IRect rect;
    };
    std::optional<Placement> add(IVec2 size);                   // nullopt if larger than a page
    int page_count() const;
    void clear();
};
```

#### class `AtlasSet`

```cpp
class AtlasSet {                                                // App resource (RenderPlugin)
public:
    explicit AtlasSet(int page_size = 2048, int padding = 1);
    // Fails for images bigger than a page; keep those as standalone textures.
    Result<TextureRegion> add(AssetServer &assets, const ImageData &image,
                              StrId group = str_id("default"));
    std::span<const AssetId<Texture>> pages(StrId group) const;
    AssetId<Texture> shape_page() const;                        // first "default" page, else none (slot 0)
    int page_size() const;
};
```

### lam/render/camera.h

```cpp
#include <lam/render/camera.h>
```

Source: [`src/render/include/lam/render/camera.h`](../src/render/include/lam/render/camera.h). Namespaces: `lam`.

Camera components (presentation only, never hashed) and the per-world CameraView.

#### struct `Camera2D`

```cpp
struct Camera2D {                                               // highest priority wins per world
    Vec2 position;                                              // centre, world pixels
    float zoom = 1;                                             // pixel-perfect: snapped to n or 1/n
    float rotation = 0;
    bool pixel_snap = true;                                     // backend rounds view-space vertices
    int priority = 0;
};
```

Reflected with `LAM_REFLECT_FLAGS`: component; flags `lam::kSerialize | lam::kSnapshot`; fields `position`, `zoom`, `rotation`, `pixel_snap`, `priority`.

#### struct `CameraFollow`

Goes on the camera. Aims at the target's interpolated position + offset (the feet by default). A target with no Transform leaves the camera where it is.

```cpp
struct CameraFollow {
    Entity target;
    float half_life = 0.08f;
    float lookahead_seconds = 0;
    float lookahead_max = 0;
    float lookahead_half_life = 0.25f;
    Rect dead_zone;                                             // relative to the centre; empty = none
    float snap_distance = 128;                                  // jumps further than this snap
    bool snap_next = false;                                     // cut instead of gliding, once
    Vec2 offset;                                                // e.g. {0, -16} to aim above the feet
};
```

Reflected with `LAM_REFLECT_FLAGS`: component; flags `lam::kSerialize | lam::kSnapshot`; fields `target`, `half_life`, `lookahead_seconds`, `lookahead_max`, `lookahead_half_life`, `dead_zone`, `snap_distance`, `snap_next`, `offset`.

#### struct `CameraBounds`

Goes on the camera. Keeps the view inside `world`, centring on any axis where it doesn't fit.

### lam/render/camera_math.h

```cpp
#include <lam/render/camera_math.h>
```

Source: [`src/render/include/lam/render/camera_math.h`](../src/render/include/lam/render/camera_math.h). Namespaces: `lam`.

Camera maths. Smoothing is exponential so it looks the same at any frame rate. Non-finite input leaves the camera alone, since one NaN would stick in the smoothed position forever.

```cpp
Vec2 camera_follow_step(Vec2 camera, Vec2 target, Vec2 target_velocity, const CameraFollow &f,
                        float dt);
```

Follow with unsmoothed look-ahead. The systems use the smoothed version below.

```cpp
Vec2 clamp_to_bounds(Vec2 center, Vec2 view_size_world, const Rect &bounds);
```

Empty bounds leave `center` unchanged; an axis too small for the view centres on the bounds.

```cpp
void add_trauma(CameraShake &s, float amount);                  // clamped to [0, 1]
```

```cpp
void decay_trauma(CameraShake &s, float dt);
```

Also advances the noise clock.

```cpp
Vec2 camera_shake_offset(const CameraShake &s, std::uint32_t seed);
```

Whole world pixels. Each axis uses its own hashed value noise, so it's deterministic.

#### struct `CameraFollowState`

Added by camera_follow. Snapshotted so undo keeps the glide, but never saved. Remove it to force a snap.

```cpp
struct CameraFollowState {
    Vec2 lookahead;
    Vec2 last_target;
    bool tracking = false;                                      // false: snap next frame
};
```

```cpp
Vec2 camera_lookahead_goal(Vec2 target_velocity, const CameraFollow &f);
```

velocity \* lookahead_seconds, length capped at lookahead_max.

```cpp
Vec2 camera_lookahead_step(Vec2 lookahead, Vec2 target_velocity, const CameraFollow &f, float dt);
```

Smoothed so turning around swings the view across instead of jumping.

```cpp
Vec2 camera_follow_point(Vec2 camera, Vec2 aim, const CameraFollow &f, float dt);
```

With a dead zone the camera only chases the part of `aim` outside it. Never overshoots.

```cpp
float half_life_factor(float half_life, float dt);
```

1 - 2^(-dt / half_life), or 1 when half_life <= 0.

#### struct `ShakeAt`

Lets tick systems shake the camera without touching CameraShake:

```cpp
ctx.emit(ShakeAt{.trauma = 0.4f});
```

Adds to every CameraShake in the emitting world. Presentation only.

```cpp
struct ShakeAt {
    float trauma = 0.3f;
};
```


Source: [`src/render/include/lam/render/passes.h`](../src/render/include/lam/render/passes.h). Namespaces: `lam`.

Offscreen targets, routed by layer range so the sort key needs no pass bits. A target is composited back at a later layer of the same view. Target 0 is the virtual screen.

```cpp

```

#### struct `RenderTargetDesc`

How an offscreen target is sized, sampled when composited, and cleared.

```cpp
struct RenderTargetDesc {
    IVec2 size;                                                 // 0,0 = virtual size * virtual_scale
    float virtual_scale = 1;
    TextureFilter filter = TextureFilter::Point;
    bool clear = true;                                          // once per view
    Color clear_color = kTransparent;
};
```

#### class `RenderPasses`

```cpp
class RenderPasses {                                            // App resource
public:
    // Re-adding a name replaces its description. Returns 1..7.
    RenderTargetId add_target(StrId name, const RenderTargetDesc &d);
    RenderTargetId find(StrId name) const;                      // 0 if unknown
    // Inclusive range; target 0 sends the layers back to the screen.
    void route_layers(std::uint8_t first, std::uint8_t last, RenderTargetId target);
    // Draws `source` with `material` just before the quads of `at_layer`.
    void composite(RenderTargetId source, MaterialId material, std::uint8_t at_layer);
    RenderTargetId target_of(std::uint8_t layer) const;
    struct Composite {
        RenderTargetId source;
        MaterialId material;
        std::uint8_t layer;
    };
    std::span<const Composite> composites() const;              // sorted by layer
    static constexpr std::size_t kMaxTargets = 7;
    static constexpr std::size_t kMaxComposites = 16;
    std::size_t target_count() const;
    const RenderTargetDesc &desc(RenderTargetId id) const;
    StrId name_of(RenderTargetId id) const;
    // At least 1x1. Target 0 is the virtual screen.
    IVec2 target_size(RenderTargetId id, IVec2 virtual_size) const;
    std::uint32_t version() const;                              // backends re-create targets when it changes
};
```

Render queue. Each quad has a sort key


and a 32-bit tiebreak (entity index for y-sorted sprites, otherwise push order).



1/16 px steps over +-524288 px. Done in double because float rounds odd steps up past 2^23.

```cpp

                                      MaterialId material, std::uint16_t texture,
                                      std::uint8_t clip);
constexpr std::uint8_t key_view(std::uint64_t k);
constexpr std::uint8_t key_layer(std::uint64_t k);
constexpr MaterialId key_material(std::uint64_t k);
constexpr std::uint16_t key_texture(std::uint64_t k);
constexpr std::uint8_t key_clip(std::uint64_t k);
```

#### class `RenderQueue`

```cpp
class RenderQueue {
public:
    explicit RenderQueue(std::size_t quad_capacity = 65536);
    // One view per visible world, bottom first. Returns 0..7.
    std::uint8_t begin_view(const CameraView &view);
    void set_view(std::uint8_t view);
    std::uint8_t current_view() const;
    std::span<const CameraView> views() const;
    // Virtual pixels. 0 means no clip; up to 255 per frame.
    std::uint8_t clip(IRect virtual_rect);
    void set_clip(std::uint8_t clip);
    std::span<const IRect> clips() const;                       // clips()[id - 1]
    void set_shape_texture(AssetId<Texture> page);
    AssetId<Texture> shape_texture() const;
    // tiebreak 0 uses push order.
    void push(std::uint8_t layer, float depth, MaterialId material, AssetId<Texture> texture,
              const QuadVertex (&v)[4], std::uint32_t tiebreak = 0);
    void sprite(const Sprite &s, const Transform2D &t, std::uint32_t tiebreak = 0);
    void region(const TextureRegion &r, Vec2 position, Vec2 scale, float rotation, Vec2 pivot,
                Color tint, std::uint8_t layer, float depth, MaterialId material = 0,
                bool flip_x = false);
    void rect(Rect r, Color c, std::uint8_t layer, float depth = 0);
    void rect_lines(Rect r, float thickness, Color c, std::uint8_t layer, float depth = 0);
    void line(Vec2 a, Vec2 b, float thickness, Color c, std::uint8_t layer, float depth = 0);
    void circle(Vec2 center, float radius, Color c, std::uint8_t layer, float depth = 0);
    void ellipse(Vec2 center, Vec2 radii, Color c, std::uint8_t layer, float depth = 0);
    // Same as draw_triangle in shapes.h.
    void triangle(Vec2 a, Vec2 b, Vec2 c, Color col, std::uint8_t layer, float depth = 0);
    void light(Vec2 center, float radius, Color c, MaterialId material,
               std::uint8_t layer = kLayerLights);
    std::span<const DrawQuad> quads() const;
    std::size_t size() const;
    std::size_t capacity() const;                               // can grow past this, with a dev warning
    void clear();
};
```
